cases.name: Agnes “Aggie” McFedries Kennedy
cases.about:
If Agnes McFedries Kennedy had something she believed you liked, you may as well have considered it yours. Whether clothing or some trinket, the bubbly young mother of four and grandmother to two would not only make the other person take what she offered, but in the end leave them feeling they’d just done her a very big favor. Always neat and well-groomed, “Aggie” also had an abounding sense of humor reflecting her beauty both inside and out; her genuine, almost perpetual smile lifted the spirits of everyone she met. After graduating from Davenport Central High School, she’d gone on to Iowa State University where she earned her teaching degree. At Williams Junior High School in Davenport — where she began her teaching career — she quickly found her niche with underprivileged students and those who needed additional help. She seemed to have an uncanny ability to understand things from other people’s perspectives — whether young teens or adults — and offered her assistance and encouragement whenever it seemed appropriate. Her kindly demeanor reflected a genuine interest in the welfare of others as well as a commitment to her work.

She left an indelible mark on hundreds of young students during the years she taught school, and continued to support the underdog long after she quit teaching.

“Agnes had outrageous joy. She would come into the room and she had this smile and eyes that sparkled,” Kennedy’s sister, Kate Heuer, told WQAD News Channel 8. “She would always find humor and the happy side of everything.”

cases.name: Madeline Victoria "Maddy" Bakoylis
cases.about: Lindsey Park said she knew Maddy for "a while" and the two became better friends during the summer. "We'd help each other out," Lindsey said. "She was the type of girl who would help anyone out if she could. She was kind. "But she could be dramatic, you know? She had a big personality, in a really good way. And she always spoke what she thought. She didn't stay silent. I'm going to miss Maddy."
cases.narrative:
Jessica Bakoylis said her daughter's death was "brutal."
"They told me Maddy had a broken clavicle and there were bones broken in her neck," she said. "And she had bruising on her body. She fought whoever did this to her."
